gallery.title: File:Union Camps at Shiloh.png
gallery.artist: United States Military Academy, Department of Military Art and Engineering, with Colonel Vincent J. Esposito as the chief editor.
gallery.credit: This a modified page (image 40) of the West Point Atlas of American Wars Volume I, which can be found in the Library of Congress here.
gallery.description: This image from a West Point atlas has been rotated so north is at the top, and TwoScarsUp has added more labels to make it easier to read. (Note that the "North arrow" is not perfectly straight "up"—this is correct.) It shows the positions of the camps of the Union army on the Shiloh battlefield on April 5, 1862. The Battle of Shiloh, in the American Civil War, began on the next day.

gallery.title: File:BattleOfShilohDay1East9AM.png
gallery.artist: United States Military Academy, Department of Military Art and Engineering, with Colonel Vincent J. Esposito as the chief editor. Additional labels added by TwoScarsUp.
gallery.credit: This a modified and cropped file from page (image 42) of the West Point Atlas of American Wars Volume I, which can be found in the Library of Congress here.
gallery.description: This image from a West Point atlas has been rotated so north is at the top, and TwoScarsUp has added more labels to make it easier to read. (Note that the "North arrow" is not perfectly straight "up"—this is correct.) The original atlas page has been cropped to focus on the east side of the battlefield. The map shows the positions of the Union and Confederate armies on the Shiloh battlefield around 9:00 AM on April 6, 1862.  The location of the Sunken Road and the Peach Orchard are based on text and maps in "Shiloh and the Western Campaign of 1862" by O. Edward Cunningham found on pages 240 and 267.

The map shows the positions of the Union and Confederate armies on the west side of the Shiloh battlefield around 9:00 AM on April 6, 1862. gallery.title: File:BattleOfShilohDay1noon.png
gallery.artist: United States Military Academy, Department of Military Art and Engineering, with Colonel Vincent J. Esposito as the chief editor. Additional labels added by TwoScarsUp.
gallery.credit: This a modified and cropped file from page (image 43) of the West Point Atlas of American Wars Volume I, which can be found in the Library of Congress here.
gallery.description: This image from a West Point atlas has been rotated so north is at the top, and TwoScarsUp has added more labels to make it easier to read. (Note that the "North arrow" is not perfectly straight "up"—this is correct.) The map shows the positions of the Union and Confederate armies on the Shiloh battlefield around noon on April 6, 1862.  The locations of the Crossroads and the Sunken Road are based on maps in "Shiloh and the Western Campaign of 1862" by O. Edward Cunningham including the map on page 220 and text on page 240. West Point's positioning of the Union troops agrees with Cunningham's text on pages 222 and 223.

gallery.title: File:BattleOfShilohDay1priorto4pm.png
gallery.artist: United States Military Academy (a.k.a. "West Point"), Department of Military Art and Engineering, with Colonel Vincent J. Esposito as the chief editor. Additional labels added by TwoScarsUp.
gallery.credit: This a modified and cropped file from page (image 44) of the West Point Atlas of American Wars Volume I, which can be found in the Library of Congress here.
gallery.description: This image is from a West Point atlas that has been rotated so north is at the top, and TwoScarsUp has added more labels to make it easier to read. (Note that the "North arrow" is not perfectly straight "up"—this is correct.) The map shows the positions of the Union and Confederate armies on the Shiloh battlefield just before 4:00 pm on April 6, 1862. The locations of the Crossroads and the Hornets Nest are based on maps in "Shiloh and the Western Campaign of 1862" by O. Edward Cunningham on pages 220 and 239. West Point's positioning of the Union troops agrees with Cunningham's map on page 260. The West Point text has McArthur moving back to the Landing around 3:00 pm, but Cunningham writes that this happened when Hurlbut moved back around 4:00 pm.

gallery.title: File:BattleOfShilohGrantSituation.png
gallery.artist: TwoScarsUp
gallery.description: This is an assessment of Major General Grant's situation at almost noon on the first day of fighting of the Battle of Shiloh in the American Civil War. Sources are "Shiloh and the Western Campaign of 1862", by O. Edward Cunningham; and "Shiloh" by Larry J. Daniel. Specific pages are Cunningham pages 236, 247, 247, and 238. Daniel pages 202-203. Cunningham p. 201-202, 241, 208, 208, 211-212, 211-212. Daniel p. 174. Cunningham p.160, 160, 316.

gallery.title: File:BattleOfShilohGrantsLastLine.png
gallery.artist: Hlj (Hal Jesperson) made original. Original has been cropped by TwoScarsUp to focus on Grant's Last Line.
gallery.credit: This file is a crop from the file "Shiloh Battle April 6 pm.png" created by Hal Jesperson.
gallery.description: Grant assigned Colonel Joseph D. Webster the task of setting up a defensive position at Pittsburg Landing on the first day (April 6, 1862) of the Battle of Shiloh in the American Civil War. Webster organized artillery and stragglers into a defensive position on a ridge. The position held. The map is comparable to Map 12, page 247, in "Shiloh" by Larry J. Daniel.

gallery.title: File:BattleOfShilohBeauregard.png
gallery.artist: TwoScarsUp
gallery.description: This is an assessment of General Beauregard's situation at the end of the first day of fighting of the Battle of Shiloh in the American Civil War. Sources are mostly "Shiloh" by Larry J. Daniel. Smaller contributions are from "Shiloh and the Western Campaign of 1862", by O. Edward Cunningham; and "Battle Cry of Freedom" by James McPherson. Specific pages are Daniel p. 251, 254, 256, 256, 265, 227, 263, and 251. Cunningham p. 325. Also Daniel p. 251, 251, 251, 232 & 251, 250, 250, and 112. Also McPherson p. 412. Also Daniel p.262.

gallery.title: File:Shiloh battlefield topical map V2.png
gallery.artist: The file, created in 1920, is from the Shiloh National Military Park. Additional labels added by TwoScarsUp.
gallery.credit: This a modified and cropped file called "Map of the Battlefield of Shiloh",  which can be found in the Library of Congress here.
gallery.description: This is an image from a Shiloh National Military Park map, and TwoScarsUp has added more labels to make it easier to read. The map shows places of importance, including field names, on the Shiloh battlefield. The battle took place on April 6 & 7, 1862.  The locations of the Crossroads, Peach Orchard, Hornet's Nest, and Grant's Last Line are based on maps in "Shiloh and the Western Campaign of 1862" by O. Edward Cunningham, including the maps on pages 220, 239, 267, and 328.  The location of the Bloody Pond is shown on a map on page 14 of Jeff Shaara's "Civil War Battlefields".
